text:
sasha_support: heads up — multiple customers reporting a sudden spike of 502/503s from Hosted API (/v1/generate) starting ~2026-03-17T09:12Z. forwarding an example from a customer (AtlasHealth) — they see `503` with body `{"error":"control_plane_dep_unavailable"}`

jordan_oncall: on it. pulling control-plane logs and gateway traces now. any repro steps from support ticket?

sasha_support: forwarded their curl repro, they did a simple call and got 503 consistently for ~5 requests, then 2nd attempt succeeded after ~12s. here's their request: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' 
 -d '{"model":"rwd-instruct-1","input":"summarize ..."}'
```

maria_sre: looking at gateway -> routing-policy svc traces: latency spike around 09:11-09:20Z. routing-policy returned 500/502 to gateway intermittently, also seeing 504s when routing-policy talks to config-db. config-db client logs show connection pool exhaustion (max connections reached).

lee_engine: FYI there was a routing-policy rollout at 09:05 with a change to stickiness TTL + new query that fans out to config DB. rolling it gradually, but looks like the change increased DB load.

konrad_prod: auth/session service also shows increased session fetch failures (timeouts) around same window — likely due to config-db slowness. sample from auth logs: 
```
[auth-session] ERROR fetchSession timeout=2000ms trace=svc=auth-session tid=ab12cd status=504 err="pg timeout: canceling statement due to statement timeout"
```

jordan_oncall: summary: routing-policy change caused heavier DB fanout -> config-db pool exhaustion -> auth/session and routing-policy returned 5xx -> gateway surfaced 5xx to customers. mitigation options: rollback routing-policy, increase config-db pool temporarily, enable routing-policy fallback to cached routes, clear session cache for impacted tenants.

sasha_support: customers asking about billing and SLA impact. any ETA on mitigation?

jordan_oncall: immediate plan implemented: 1) trigger rollback of routing-policy rollout 2) bump connection pool to 120 for config-db (short window) 3) enable fast-path fallback in gateway for routing-policy errors 4) clear auth session cache for the top 5 affected tenants.

deploy-bot: rollback job queued: routing-policy v3.2.1 -> v3.2.0 (job id rb-238910-17).

maria_sre: rolled back routing-policy to v3.2.0 at 09:26Z. config-db pool increased at 09:27Z. enabling fallback at 09:28Z. watching metrics.

jordan_oncall: after rollback and pool bump, 5xxs dropped to baseline by ~09:30Z. latency normalized. routing-policy error rate went from 18% -> 0.8%.

sasha_support: customer (AtlasHealth) confirms their calls started succeeding at 09:35Z after retries. no billing adjustments requested yet, but they asked for a timeline and RCA.

lee_engine: follow-ups: revert the stickiness TTL change and rewrite the fanout query to avoid per-request fanout to config-db, add a local cache in routing-policy for TTL-consistent entries.

konrad_prod: runbook item: add circuit-breaker on routing-policy -> config-db path, emit pool-exhaustion alerts sooner, and add synthetic checks that exercise routing-policy read path under low QPS.

jordan_oncall: filing postmortem and follow-up tasks. created PM ticket PM-2026-042 and linked deploy rollback job and metrics.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-015 created and assigned to eng-sre.

maria_sre: scheduling capacity test for config-db and a controlled canary rollout for routing-policy change with stricter telemetry checks.

jordan_oncall: closing this escalation thread for now — monitoring for 1h. ping here if anything resurfaces :white_check_mark:
